title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1966-07-03

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with good‑to‑excellent clarity captures a raw, upbeat 1966 set highlighted by He Was A Friend Of Mine and Viola Lee Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that most listeners describe as crisp and surprisingly clean for an early‑'66 tape.  The performance itself is full of youthful energy – Jerry’s trippy vocal intros, tight harmonies on Dancin’ In The Streets, and a punchy, fast‑paced Viola Lee Blues are repeatedly praised, while Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming gets special mention on that track.  A few reviewers note occasional cut‑offs or missing songs, but the overall impression is that this early show delivers raw emotion and strong set flow.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (≈80%) are 4‑5 stars, emphasizing excellent sound quality and standout early‑Dead performances; only a handful of lower ratings mention minor cut‑offs or missing tracks.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Described as ‘nice’, ‘great’, and ‘excellent’ sound quality with crisp vocals; occasional fade‑ins/cut‑offs noted but no major distortion.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑summer 1966 set is upbeat and raw, with tight vocal harmonies and fast‑paced blues numbers; despite a few missing cuts, the flow feels energetic and representative of the band’s pre‑psychedelic era.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His trippy spoken intro on Viola Lee Blues and ‘fluttering’ vocal style are highlighted; praised for kind vocals and youthful energy.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming is singled out as standing out on Viola Lee Blues.
